summary.intent: Fix pre-existing TypeScript type errors across the web app and load test packages in the cipher-box monorepo.
summary.outcome: All type errors resolved: web app errors were caused by stale package builds (fixed by rebuilding @cipherbox/crypto and @cipherbox/api-client), and the load test error was a scoping issue with `cid` declared inside a `try` block but referenced in `finally`.

repo: Type errors in web app imports (missing exports like deriveVaultKeyIpnsKeypair, deriveByoConfigIpnsKeypair, teeControllerConnectionTest) can be caused by stale package builds rather than missing source code — always rebuild dependent packages before diagnosing missing export errors.
The monorepo has at least two buildable packages that web depends on: @cipherbox/crypto and @cipherbox/api-client, both requiring explicit rebuilds to regenerate declaration files.

code.finding: `cid` was declared with `let` inside the `try` block but referenced in the `finally` block. TypeScript treats `finally` as a sibling scope to `try`, not nested within it, so the variable must be declared before the `try` block to be accessible in `finally`.

workflow: In a pnpm monorepo, type errors in consuming packages after adding or renaming exports in a library package are often resolved by rebuilding the library (`pnpm --filter <package> build`) rather than modifying source code.
TypeScript scoping: variables declared with `let` inside a `try` block are not accessible in the corresponding `finally` block — declare them before the `try` if they need to be used in `finally`.

friction: The root cause of web app type errors (stale builds) was non-obvious and required multiple grep/read steps before the rebuild hypothesis was tested.
The `cid` scoping issue required several re-reads of the same file (4+ times) to correctly identify the try/finally scope boundary.
